title: How to Invite Your Teen Into Screen-Free Time Without Making It a Contest
summary: Offer teen-chosen shared leisure without turning it into a screen-time battle: protect online commitments, make small invitations, accept refusals, and adjust together.
seo_description: How to invite a teen into shared screen-free time without forcing a game night: respect online ties, handle refusals, and try small low-cost choices today.
release_move: The parent keeps separate safety and household boundaries, while the teen can choose, change, decline, or end an ordinary shared leisure activity without punishment.

core_belief_shift.from: I need to replace my teen's screen time with family activities they will eventually enjoy.
core_belief_shift.to: I can offer small shared activities that fit their interests and let them refuse, while handling necessary limits separately.

book_relevance.reason: The Social Playbook Chapter 3 contains a board-game example and perspective-taking premise; this parent guide adapts only the ethical, consent-respecting part, not its bait framing or scientific authority.

hero.alt: A teenager chooses the next card while a parent listens beside him at their kitchen table.

social_image.alt: A teen leads a relaxed card game at home while his parent pays attention.
